text-secondary.comment: Secondary or supporting text — labels, captions, instructional copy. Legible at a glance, subordinate to default ink.

text-muted.comment: Tertiary or de-emphasized text — fine print, nested meta, quiet instrument chrome.

accent.comment: Buttons, sliders, links, focus rings, dropdown hover/inset accent. Domain: chrome (operating controls) — never read by work-surface code.

accent-secondary.comment: Secondary button/control accent — a second chrome hue for an action that needs visual weight but isn't the primary CTA. Same shade-band convention as chrome.accent (700 light / 600 dark) so it shares --chrome-ink without needing its own ink token.

accent-tertiary.comment: Tertiary button/control accent, third chrome hue. Same shade-band convention as chrome.accent. Note: shares its light-mode step (purple.700) with work-surface.relation — a tuning candidate, not yet resolved.

accent-text.comment: Chrome-accent used AS text/border directly on a neutral surface (outline-button text, links, eyebrow labels) rather than as a fill. Distinct from accent because a fill needs to be dark enough to pair with fixed --chrome-ink, while standalone text needs to be light enough to read against the page itself — in light theme one value satisfies both (reuses accent's value here), but they diverge in dark theme. See design-tokens/README.md > "Fill tokens need an ink pair".

ink.comment: Text/icon colour for content sitting on a chrome-accent fill (filled buttons, active slider handles). Chrome-accent's fill is dark-toned in both themes, so unlike the neutral text roles this does not invert with theme — it stays a fixed light ink. Also used by accent-secondary and accent-tertiary, which were deliberately chosen at matching luminance so one ink token covers all three.

idle.comment: Available but unselected points, edges, or objects.

active.comment: Selected, current, or provisional/preview geometry. Shares a hue with hover by deliberate choice; distinguished by size/weight/dash treatment instead of colour.

relation.comment: A second object referenced against the active one — comparison, not selection.

emphasis.comment: Rare warm or editorial highlight. Never the default selection colour.

critical.comment: Destructive, critical, or irreversible action — deliberately deeper than the base red.

critical-ink.comment: Text/icon colour for content sitting on a critical fill (danger-button hover, alert banners). Critical is a fixed red.500 in both themes and reads better with dark text than light, so — like chrome.ink — this stays fixed rather than inverting with theme.

critical-text.comment: Critical used AS text/border directly on a neutral surface (danger-outline buttons, error copy) rather than as a fill. --critical is a fixed red.500 in both themes, which happens to pass as text against the dark surface (~4.6:1) but fails against the light one (~3.3:1) — the reverse of chrome's problem, but the same root cause: a value tuned for one role doesn't automatically work for the other. red.700 restores light-theme contrast to ~7:1.

text-secondary.comment: Secondary or supporting text — labels, captions, instructional copy. Legible at a glance, subordinate to default ink.

text-muted.comment: Tertiary or de-emphasized text — fine print, nested meta, quiet instrument chrome.

accent.comment: Buttons, sliders, links, focus rings, dropdown hover/inset accent. Domain: chrome (operating controls) — never read by work-surface code.

accent-secondary.comment: Secondary button/control accent — a second chrome hue for an action that needs visual weight but isn't the primary CTA. Same shade-band convention as chrome.accent (700 light / 600 dark) so it shares --chrome-ink without needing its own ink token.

accent-tertiary.comment: Tertiary button/control accent, third chrome hue. Same shade-band convention as chrome.accent.

accent-text.comment: Chrome-accent used AS text/border directly on a neutral surface (outline-button text, links, eyebrow labels) rather than as a fill. blue.600 (accent's own dark value) is 3.0:1 against --neutral-surface-bg as text — fails WCAG AA. blue.400 is ~6.4:1. A fill needs to be dark enough to pair with fixed --chrome-ink; standalone text needs the opposite (light enough to read against a near-black page) — the two constraints are mutually exclusive in dark theme, hence two tokens. See design-tokens/README.md > "Fill tokens need an ink pair".

accent-secondary-text.comment: accent-secondary's text/border counterpart — see accent-text. green.600 is 3.0:1 as text; green.400 is ~6.4:1.

accent-tertiary-text.comment: accent-tertiary's text/border counterpart — see accent-text. purple.600 is 3.0:1 as text; purple.400 is ~6.4:1.

Also used by accent-secondary and accent-tertiary, which were deliberately chosen at matching luminance so one ink token covers all three.
